subject: Finding a stable version of R, TMB etc

messages.author: 216ff7e50db41ce5
messages.subject: Finding a stable version of R, TMB etc
parts:
Hi

I am really stuck.

 

Many researchers at IHME use TMB for large models in R. They have been using the following set of versions for some time because we have not been able to find another set that “works:”

 

  1. R  3.6
  2. TMB 1.7.16
  3. The symbolic analysis fix
  4. Gcc 4.7
  5. Linux

I could get a more precise version set if you need it, although due to a lost backup I don’t have the dockerfile for this image.

 

We build a docker image from a docker file, and then convert to a singularity image, and run it on our Ubuntu/Slurm cluster.

 

We need the speed-optimization provided by runSymbolicAnalysis (RSA)so that our models converge in a practical amount of time. The test model I use converges in 73 minutes using the above configuration. Without RSA it is still running after 24 hours, when I deliberately time it out.

 

I have been able to build images that “work” (meaning that they don’t stop with an error) using later versions of R and TMB, but I have never been able to find a set of versions where our test model converges, or that work with RSA

 

My latest attempt:

 

  1. R 4.2.3
  2. TMB 1.9.4 (which I believe is the latest)
  3. RSA
  4. The gnu threading libraries. I tried Intel’s TBB library but could not get past a missing symbol error.

 

I can provide a Dockerfile for this version. When I ran our test model it errored after 8.5 hours with a division by zero error in Newton’s method.

 

Can someone please provide me with a set of versions that works? Or advice? Otherwise we will be stuck on R 3.6 and TMB 1.7.16

 

Cheers

Geoff
